title: Schema Basics
description: Learn the fundamentals of GraphQL schemas in Hot Chocolate.

data.text: The GraphQL schema is the heart of your API. It defines what data is available, how it's structured, and how clients can query it.
Hot Chocolate supports both **schema-first** (write SDL, generate C#) and **code-first** (write C#, generate schema) approaches. Most .NET teams prefer code-first.

cards.title: Schema-First
cards.description: Write .graphql SDL files, then generate C# types.

cards.title: Code-First
cards.description: Write C# classes, Hot Chocolate generates the schema.

data.text: In code-first, you use attributes to shape the schema. The `[GraphQL]` attribute on a class makes it a type, and `[Query]` exposes methods.

data.title: Schema Streaming
data.text: Hot Chocolate can stream your schema as SDL at /graphql?sdl. This is useful for GraphQL IDEs and code generation tools.

terms.definition: A contract that defines the types, queries, and mutations available in a GraphQL API.
Schema Definition Language — a human-readable way to describe a GraphQL schema.
An approach where C# code generates the GraphQL schema.
An approach where you write GraphQL SDL and generate C# types from it.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: The schema is the contract between server and client
Hot Chocolate supports both schema-first and code-first
Attributes like [GraphQL] and [Query] shape the schema
